title: Captain Kind and the Great World Wobble

storyteller.name: Storyteller
storyteller.description: Warm, soothing adult storyteller who reads the book and answers the kids' questions

kid_older.name: Leo (Age 8)
kid_older.description: Curious 8-year-old who asks about the plot and loves guessing mysteries

kid_younger.name: Mia (Age 5)
kid_younger.description: Playful 5-year-old who notices funny and cute visual details, giggles and gasps

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Join the kindness crew! Today we're reading Captain Kind and the Great World Wobble. Can you spot something round that might wobble?

lines.speaker: kid_younger
lines.text: My round little cheeks! <giggle>

lines.speaker: kid_older
lines.text: I'm ready to look for clues. What could make a whole world wobble?

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Let's open our book and find out together.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: At supper, one pea bounced off Captain Kind’s spoon. Then every pea bounced—boing, boing, boing!

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: “Stay for supper!” giggled the captain.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Outside, balls and oranges bounced too. Even the moon bobbed above the roofs.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Captain Kind tied the towel cape: “A wobble needs a helper!”

lines.speaker: kid_older
lines.text: Could Captain Kind help by catching the bouncy things? What would you try?

lines.speaker: kid_younger
lines.text: Even the moon! Can you point to it if you want? Does it need a tiny cape?

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: That moon does look ready for a wobbling adventure. Catching is an idea we can watch for. Let's see what our towel-caped helper tries.

pages.qa_grounding: the moon bobbed above the roofs

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Captain Kind held a basket under the bouncing oranges. Boing, they popped right out again!

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: “Catching won’t stop this wobble,” said the captain.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Captain Kind put an ear to the grass. “Hic!” said the ground—and up went every round thing.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: “The world has hiccups!” whispered the captain.

lines.speaker: kid_older
lines.text: The ground said hic! Was listening the clue Captain Kind needed?

lines.speaker: kid_younger
lines.text: A teeny pebble bounced too! Hic. Can we do a quiet hic together?

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Yes, listening helped the captain discover the world's hiccups. You can whisper a little hic, or just listen. I wonder what gentle help the captain will try.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: “When I have hiccups, I take a quiet pause,” said Captain Kind. So the captain sat beside the bouncing ball.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: “Pause with me, little world.”

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: “And a little sip of water feels nice.” Captain Kind brought a jug and cups for the neighbors.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: “Your own cup, a little sip—come sit with me.”

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: One neighbor called another, and another brought a cushion. Soon the street was sitting together.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: “Room for you, a sip for you, a pause for everyone.”

lines.speaker: kid_younger
lines.text: A cushion for a bottom! <giggle> Could I help by making room beside me?

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Yes, making room is a lovely kindness. You can point to a cushion, if you like. I'll take an easy breath in and let it out softly. A pretend sip is welcome, too.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: “Breathe in, like smelling a flower.” “Breathe out, like cooling your soup.”

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Together they breathed, slow and soft—and the bouncing grew smaller.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: The peas rested, the balls rested, and the oranges rested. The moon gave one last tiny hic!

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Then it settled into a cloud, and everyone whispered, “Good night, world.”

lines.speaker: kid_older
lines.text: That last hic was so small! Did all those little kindnesses help everyone settle together?

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: They did. The neighbors made room, shared water, and paused together. Now the round things are resting, and even the moon has settled into a cloud.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Captain Kind hung up the towel cape and snuggled into bed. “A little kindness brought us together,” the captain murmured.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Outside, the world was still, and inside, the captain slept.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Our kindness crew can rest now, too. What tiny kindness could you share tomorrow? Say it, point, or think it quietly.

lines.speaker: kid_younger
lines.text: I could make room for someone beside me. A cozy little space.

lines.speaker: kid_older
lines.text: I could listen when someone needs a helper. Even a quiet helper counts.

lines.speaker: storyteller
lines.text: Small kindnesses can bring us together. Subscribe and come back for our next story. Good night, kindness crew.
